blindSummary:
This state/province is geographically attributable as the institutional home of the official national assembly of traditional leaders' formal campaign against constitutional equality for queer people. That body - the country's official house of tribal chiefs - met at a town in this state/province and resolved that 'traditional leaders are disappointed that this immoral practice has been given a lifeline by our courts', and separately asked the national legislature to review the constitutional clause protecting against discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation. Commentary in a national magazine identified this lobbying, together with anti-gay statements by the chair of a constitutional-review committee, as precisely the mechanism that 'intensifies prejudice and hatred' and fuels homophobic violence - an identified official-climate pathway, not merely a statement.

The dossier notes this evidence dates from 2010-2016 and should be treated as durable climate rather than current enacted policy. No provincial statute, no enforcement against a visitor, and no trans-specific incident series is documented. This state/province is not listed in the former-ethnic-homeland traditional-court geography; its risk signal is the formal institutional position taken on its soil, not a parallel legal system operating on visitors. The national constitution, the equality statute, and the hate-crime framework remain uniform and protective.
blindSourceSummaries: Published letter (June 2010) from the official national house of traditional leaders and its provincial houses after meeting at a town in this state/province: while 'respecting' the constitutional court's same-sex-marriage judgment, 'traditional leaders are disappointed that this immoral practice has been given a lifeline by our courts'; states they do not support legalisation of same-sex marriages, warns of ostracism and violence, and vows a five-year campaign against it.

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (missing from cache); the underlying 2016 report documents the national traditional-leaders body asking the national legislature to review the constitutional clause protecting people against discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation.

National magazine commentary (25 May 2012; a journalist interviewing a constitutional-law professor): as the traditional-leaders body lobbies to remove gay rights from the constitution and the chair of a constitutional-review committee makes anti-gay statements, lesbians and gay men continue to be subject to violent attacks - citing two corrective-rape murders (2008 and 2011) - with the traditional-leader lobbying identified as the fuel that fires homophobia.
blindTangential: The traditional-leaders campaign targets the constitutional sexual-orientation equality clause and 'same-sex marriage' - an LGBT-broad official-climate signal rather than a trans-specific measure; its documented spill-over is onto homophobic violence generally.
